thread:
alex: Ran a full run of gpu-probe + autotune on staging-gpu-pool. Some A100s (SXM) are not taking the tensor-core matmul path for short sequences (<=128). Perf regressed ~2x for small-seq workloads. Logs attached below.

alex: probe output snippet:
```
Device 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, compute=8.0, sm_count=108
flags: supports_tf32=true, supports_bf16=true, supports_fp8=false
driver_api: cudaGetDeviceProperties -> major=8 minor=0
nvml: sm_version=8.0
```

alex: autotune decision: seq=64 -> picked matmul_fp32_no_tc, seq>=512 -> matmul_tc. Expected matmul_tc for seq=64 on these cards. Microprofiling: seq=64: matmul_no_tc 0.83 ms / it (1.2k tokens/s); matmul_tc 0.25 ms / it (3.8k tokens/s) on same node when forced. So detection/heuristic mismatch.

sam: can you paste the raw probe log? maybe the feature bit for "hasTensorCoresForFP16" is missing for some kernels.

alex: pasted minimal raw logs above. Full log uploaded to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/staging/gpu-probe/1754287382.log

maria: AFAIK compute capability 8.0 should have tensor cores, but not all tensor core ops get used automatically. Our kernel selector currently checks (compute_cap >= 80) && (driver_has_bf16 || driver_tf32) but maybe the autotune also checks occupancy_estimate and rejects TC if it thinks warp occupancy too low for short matrices.

jing: we've seen CUDA driver versions where cuBLAS/cuDNN report limited tensor core support until a small runtime microkernel is JITted. Might be a race where the first run picks a non-TC kernel until the JIT finishes.

theo: suggestion: add a tiny runtime microbenchmark at startup to validate the tensor-core path. e.g. a single 100x100 fp16 gemm timed and compared to known TC baseline.

alex: microbenchmark I ran (python/pytorch):
```
import torch
x=torch.randn(8,128,512,dtype=torch.float16,device='cuda')
for _ in range(10): torch.matmul(x,x.transpose(-1,-2))
torch.cuda.synchronize()
# measure 200 iters
```
For nodes that picked no-tc we can force torch.cuda.set_enabled_lms(False) and then the TC kernel runs and perf matches expected.

sam: could be driver/CUDA mismatch on older images. What CUDA + driver are those nodes running?

alex: most are CUDA 11.4 + driver 470.x on the problematic pool. Working pool is CUDA 11.7 + driver 510.x.

maria: OK that's a red flag. 11.4 has incomplete TF32/BF16 plumbing in libnccl/cuBLAS on certain A100 revs. We should treat driver<11.6 as potentially missing runtime TC availability for some kernels.

jing: in the short-term we should: 1) add probe to surface driver+cuda runtime versions in autotune metadata, 2) update kernel selector to fallback to an explicit microbenchmark-based decision when driver < 11.6 or when compute_cap in [80, 86] but flags ambiguous.

theo: long-term: make autotuner persist per-node kernel map (immutable id per GPU image) and invalidate when driver or kernel libs update.

priya: can we canary the change? i suggest 5% traffic on dedicated pools and 10% on staging to validate no regressions.

ci-bot: autotune PR created -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6321. Contains: probe-driver-version, startup microbenchmark, per-node kernel-map caching, fallback heuristics.

alex: I'll take PR review. Also adding a small test to the perf harness to detect this case: run short-seq workload under both forced-no-tc and force-tc and assert tc throughput > no-tc * 1.6 on A100-class devices.

maria: one more gotcha: BF16/FP8 support detection. fp8 is often only available via explicit cuBLASLt APIs and on newer drivers. Our flag detection currently reads a single NVML field; let's expand to query cuBLASLt and run a 1-iter fp8 matmul probe when requested.

sam: noted. I'll add a small cwrapper that calls cublasLtGetSupportedAlgos and returns supported datatypes.

alex: timeline: I'll land the probe metadata + fallback heuristics this week, microbenchmark + perf tests next week, then canary on Friday if all green.

theo: thanks — this explains the perf spike in last night's canary. TL;DR: don't trust compute_cap alone, validate runtime capability and add a quick microbenchmark for short-seq paths.

priya: :thumbsup: schedule the canary and ping me once PR merges.

alex: will do. cc @eng-sre for node image upgrade plan.
